facts.text: Naples, Maine was named after Naples, Italy, and incorporated March 4, 1834, pulling land from four neighboring towns.
In the 19th century, famous writers Henry Wadsworth Longfellow and Nathaniel Hawthorne visited Naples, drawn by its lake scenery.
The Bay of Naples Inn opened in 1899 with 80 rooms, became a popular resort until it closed in 1951 and was razed in 1964.
A canning factory and cooperage were established in Naples village, marking early industrial activity in the town.
The Songo Lock, completed two years before Naples incorporated, linked Long Lake and Brandy Pond to Sebago Lake, enabling boat travel to Portland.
Naples sits on several water bodies, including Sebago Lake, Long Lake, Brandy Pond, and Trickey Pond, giving it a lake‑rich landscape.
